sentences.text: Every new scientific answer seems to bring both clarity and fresh mystery.
Some believe science has given us a much better understanding of the world, while others believe it has revealed how infinitely complex the world really is.
I believe both views are true, and that science deepens our understanding and our sense of complexity at the same time.
First, science has clearly given us a far better understanding of the world.
Things once seen as mysteries, like disease and weather, now have clear explanations.
For example, we now understand that illness comes from germs rather than from curses or bad air.
This shows that science has replaced confusion and fear with real, reliable knowledge.
Such understanding has let us cure illness, predict storms, and travel into space.
We grasp far more about how the world works than any earlier generation did.
In this sense, the first view is plainly correct.
Second, however, the more science learns, the more complex the world appears.
Each discovery tends to reveal deeper layers and harder questions beneath it.
Consider how studying the atom uncovered a strange quantum world that still puzzles the experts.
Such findings show that science can expand mystery even as it expands knowledge.
Fields like biology and the universe turn out to be far more intricate than people once believed.
Every answer, in other words, seems to open the door to new and harder questions.
The second view, then, is just as true as the first.
In conclusion, science has genuinely given us a clearer understanding of the world.
But it has also revealed how endlessly complex that world really is.
Science deepens both our knowledge and our wonder, and that is the true mark of discovery.
